issues.issue: This recital states the Depositor "is the owner of the Trust Fund that is hereby conveyed to the Trustee," which cannot be squared with Section 2.01 and Section 2.06, under which the conveyance is made by separate operative granting clauses and the Special Deposit is transferred by EMC rather than the Depositor. A party could argue the recital controls the scope of what passed to the Trustee.

The REMIC I pool is described as the Mortgage Loans "and certain other related assets subject to this Agreement," a phrase with no ascertainable boundary, followed by a closed list of exclusions. Which trust assets fall inside REMIC I is left to construction.

The provision invokes Treasury Regulation Section 1.860G-1(a)(4)(ii) while the accompanying maturity-date designation and every parallel REMIC paragraph invoke Section 1.860G-1(a)(4)(iii). The mismatched citation changes which regulatory safe harbor is being satisfied.

The paragraph makes the REMIC III election but designates the segregated pool of REMIC II Regular Interests as "REMIC II" rather than REMIC III. As written, two different asset pools bear the same designation.

The Class R-3 Certificates are said to be the sole class of Residual Interests in "REMIC II," although the definition of Class R-3 Certificate makes them the residual interest in REMIC III and the Class R-2 Certificates already hold REMIC II's residual. The designation contradicts itself.

Every defined term is made defeasible by the phrase "unless the context otherwise requires," with no guide to when context displaces a definition. That qualifier is itself the ground on which a party can argue a defined term does not mean what Article I says.

"Accepted Master Servicing Practices" is measured by the "customary mortgage servicing practices of prudent mortgage servicing institutions" in the relevant jurisdiction, a standard the Agreement never fixes or benchmarks. The parenthetical carve-out "(except in its capacity as successor to a Servicer)" further leaves unclear which standard governs when the Master Servicer succeeds a Servicer.

"Adjustment Date" is fixed as the first day of the month in which the Mortgage Rate changes, which may not be the adjustment date actually stated in the related Mortgage Note. Which date governs rate resets is therefore open to argument.

"Appraised Value" uses the refinancing appraisal alone for refinance loans but the lesser of appraisal and sales price for other loans, whereas the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement defines "Value" as always the lesser of appraisal and sales price. The two measures drive different loan-to-value figures for the same loans.

The definition identifies the underlying Accredited and WMC purchase and warranties agreements as "each between the Sponsor and Accredited" and "each between the Sponsor and WMC," while the bring-down letters it lists in the same clauses are with EMC. Which entity made the incorporated originator representations is left contradictory.

Certificate Principal Balance is increased by Subsequent Recoveries "pursuant to Section 5.04(b)," but Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex and loss/recovery allocation is dealt with in Article VI. The cross-reference does not lead to any recovery mechanic.

The Class A-3 Certificate is defined as representing the right to the Percentage Interest of "distributions provided for the Class A-2 Certificates," not the Class A-3 Certificates. On its face the definition gives Class A-3 holders another class's distribution entitlement.

This definition reduces the Stated Principal Balance for "Realized Losses incurred during the prior calendar month," whereas the parallel Class M-1, M-2, M-3 and M-5 definitions use Realized Losses incurred "during the related Prepayment Period." The two measurement periods produce different principal distribution amounts.

Clause (x) lists the Class A, M-1, M-2, M-4 and M-5 Principal Distribution Amounts but omits the Class M-3 Principal Distribution Amount, although clause (y)(4) still accounts for the Class M-3 balance after its distribution. The omission changes the remaining Principal Distribution Amount available to Class M-6.

The Class P Certificate Account is said to be established "pursuant to Section 6.09 hereof," but the Agreement's Article VI ends at Section 6.08, which is itself captioned "Class P Certificate Account." The account's governing section is left uncertain.

Compensating Interest is capped at the Servicing Fee for the related Servicer, but the proviso makes the Master Servicer liable "to the extent provided in Section 6.02(b)" without saying whether the same cap limits the Master Servicer's payment. Whether the Master Servicing Fee or the Servicing Fee bounds that backstop is left open.

The definition begins with an unnumbered clause for the Trustee and then a clause "(11)" for the Securities Administrator, and adds a third address "except for purposes of certificate transfer purposes." Which office is the Corporate Trust Office for a given notice or transfer is left to construction.

The Countrywide Servicing Agreement is described as being "between the Sponsor and Countrywide," while the Countrywide Assignment Agreement that assigns it to the Trust is among EMC, Countrywide and the Trustee. Which entity held the servicing agreement being assigned is inconsistent.

The Depository Agreement is described as "the agreement between the Trust and the initial Depository," although the Trust is not a contracting entity and the DTC letter of representations at Exhibit H is executed by the transaction parties. Who is bound by that agreement is unclear.

The Distribution Account is said to be created and maintained "pursuant to Section 5.08," but Article V contains no Section 5.08 and the Distribution Account is the subject of Section 5.02. The governing section for the account is misidentified.

The last sentence authorizes amendment of the rating requirements "[n]otwithstanding Section 12.01" and without Certificateholder consent, which cannot be squared with the amendment procedure and consent protections of Section 12.01. A court would have to decide which controls an amendment affecting account eligibility.

The carve-out excludes loans "purchased by the Sponsor, EMC or the related Originator pursuant to or as contemplated by Section 2.03," but Section 2.03 contains only Wells Fargo's own corporate representations; the repurchase machinery sits in Section 2.02 and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement. The exclusion's reach therefore depends on reading Section 2.03 together with those provisions.

"Insurance Policy" is defined as "any insurance policy or LPMI Policy" and then as including "any replacement policy or policies for any Insurance Policies," a circular formulation with no limit on the kinds of policies captured. Whether a given policy is an Insurance Policy (and its proceeds Insurance Proceeds) is left at large.

Clause (e) captures interest on loans "repurchased by the Sponsor, Saxon (or its assignee), the Majority Class CE Certificateholder, or by the related Originator pursuant to Sections 2.02 and 2.03," omitting EMC, which is also a Seller obliged to repurchase under Section 2.02(c) and the definition of Seller. Interest recovered on an EMC repurchase is left outside Interest Funds.

Master Servicing Compensation is defined as the Master Servicing Fee "and any amounts earned on permitted investments in the Distribution Account during the Master Servicer Float Period," but the Master Servicing Fee definition already includes those same float earnings. The float income is counted twice.

The Master Servicing Fee is defined as a fee-rate calculation "and any amounts earned on permitted investments in the Distribution Account during the Master Servicer Float Period," which duplicates the second element of Master Servicing Compensation. The two definitions cannot both be given effect without paying the float income twice.

Maximum Probable Exposure is to be "calculated by the Depositor in accordance with the EMC's internal risk management process in respect of similar instruments," an external and undisclosed standard with no objective content. Nothing in the Agreement allows a reader to test the calculation.

"Mortgage" is limited to an instrument creating a "first lien on or first priority ownership interest" in the property, yet the pool expressly contains second lien Mortgage Loans (Mortgage Loan Schedule items (g) and (s), and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement's definition of Mortgage Loans). On its face no second-lien instrument is a "Mortgage" for purposes of this Agreement.

A loan not in fact transferred remains a Mortgage Loan because of "a breach of the representation contained in Section 2.03(b)(v) hereof," but Section 2.03(b) is a one-sentence survival clause with no subsection (v) and Section 2.03(a)(v) is a consents representation by Wells Fargo. The cross-reference identifies no transfer representation.

The enumerated schedule fields use "(aa)" twice (for reset periods and for the Prepayment Charge) and contain several "[reserved]" gaps, so the lettering does not identify what the Mortgage Loan Schedule must contain. Which data the schedule must carry is a matter of construction.

The swap notional amount is said to be "set forth in the related schedule set forth in Exhibit M," but the Agreement has an Exhibit M-1 (Swap Agreement) and an Exhibit M-2 (Yield Maintenance Agreement) and no Exhibit M. Which schedule supplies the notional amount is unidentified.

The independence proviso disqualifies counsel connected with "EMC, the Depositor and the Master Servicer" only, although the opening sentence permits the opinion to be given by counsel for "the Seller," a defined term that also includes the Sponsor. Counsel for the Sponsor is thus permitted where independence was meant to be required.

"Optional Termination Date" is defined purely by a 5% balance test and not by any exercise of the clean-up call, and the definite article "[t]he Distribution Date" does not say whether it is the first such date or any date meeting the test. Because the Class A, M and B Pass-Through Rates step up "for each Distribution Date thereafter," the ambiguity directly affects coupon rates.

The first sentence excludes the Class CE Certificates from having a Pass-Through Rate yet lists "the Class CE Pass-Through Rate" among the applicable rates, and the second sentence then states the Class CE Certificate has no Pass-Through Rate. The definition contradicts itself as to that class.

The proviso excluding instruments redeemable below purchase price says clause (B) does not apply to "units of money market funds pursuant to clause (v) above," but clause (v) is guaranteed reinvestment agreements and money market funds are clause (viii). The carve-out points at the wrong category of investment.

The subtraction in clause (ii) is "the sum of (a) the related Servicing Fee, (b) the Master Servicing Fee Rate and (c) the LPMI Fee," mixing a per annum rate into a sum of dollar amounts. The shortfall cannot be computed as written.

The definition ends with "or any replacement policy therefor through the related Interest Accrual Period for such Class relating to a Distribution Date," language that has no referent for "such Class" in a policy definition. Whether and for how long a replacement policy counts as a Primary Mortgage Insurance Policy is unintelligible.

Clause (d) counts the Stated Principal Balance of loans repurchased by "the Sponsor pursuant to Sections 2.02 or 2.03," omitting EMC, the other Seller obliged to repurchase under Section 2.02(c) and the definition of Seller. Principal recovered on an EMC repurchase falls outside Principal Funds.

This "Purchase Price" differs from the "Purchase Price" separately defined in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement, which nets Servicing Advances and Advances only where the purchaser is also the servicer and awards predatory-lending damages to the Purchaser rather than the Trust. Since repurchases are made under that agreement but the price is deposited under this one, the two definitions must be reconciled.

REMIC I is defined as "the segregated pool of assets described in the Preliminary Statement and Section 6.07(a)," the identical formula used for REMIC II, so the cross-reference does not distinguish the two pools. Which assets constitute REMIC I must be worked out from elsewhere.

A REMIC Opinion must say the action "will not have an adverse effect on any REMIC created hereunder," without specifying the kind of adverse effect (loss of REMIC status, a prohibited transactions tax, or any economic detriment). The trigger for delivering, and the sufficiency of, such an opinion is left vague.

Clause (ix) requires a Replacement Mortgage Loan to "comply with each representation and warranty set forth in Section 2.03 hereof," but Section 2.03 contains only Wells Fargo's corporate representations; the loan-level warranties are in Sections 8 and 10 of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement. The substitution condition as drafted tests nothing about the replacement loan.

The Reserve Fund is said to be created "pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof," while Section 4.22(b) directs the Securities Administrator to establish the Reserve Fund on or before the Closing Date and Section 6.08 is the Class P Certificate Account. Which section governs the fund's creation and operation is contradictory.

The Saxon Assignment Agreement is said to be "attached hereto as Exhibit R-3," but Exhibit R-3 is the Wells Fargo Assignment, Assumption and Recognition Agreement per the exhibit list and the Wells Fargo Assignment Agreement definition. Two different agreements are assigned the same exhibit.

"Seller" is defined as EMC and the Sponsor, neither of which is a party to this Agreement under the preliminary paragraph, yet the Agreement imposes duties on "the Seller" (for example Section 4.20's financing-statement obligation and Section 4.02's direction right). Whether those obligations bind anyone under this instrument requires reading it against the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement.

The final sentence provides that "[n]o Servicer shall be required to make any Nonrecoverable Servicing Advances," a term the Agreement never defines; only "Nonrecoverable Advance" is defined and it addresses Advances, not Servicing Advances. The scope of the limitation is left to construction.

The single sentence runs "amounts received ... (net of expenses) or surplus amounts held ... to cover estimated expenses (including ... recoveries in respect of the representations and warranties made by the Seller pursuant to the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement) specifically related to a Mortgage Loan," so it is unclear whether repurchase-related recoveries are Subsequent Recoveries or merely an example of estimated expenses. The syntax determines whether rep-and-warranty recoveries reduce Realized Losses.

"Substitution Adjustment Amount" is given the meaning ascribed "pursuant to Section 2.03(d)," but Section 2.03 has only subsections (a) and (b) and the term is coined in an unlettered paragraph. The definitional cross-reference points to nothing.

The Tax Matters Person is "[t]he Holder of the greatest Percentage Interest" in the related class of Residual Certificates, with no tie-breaker if two holders hold equal interests and no mechanism for a change in holdings. The identity of the Tax Matters Person can therefore be indeterminate.

Prong (i)(A) measures the delinquency ratio against "31.55% of the Current Specified Enhancement Percentage" while prong (i)(B) uses "39.59%, of the Class M-1 Enhancement Percentage," and prong (ii) measures cumulative losses "as of the related Prepayment Period" rather than as of a date. Whether a Trigger Event exists turns on resolving these formulations.

Item (vi) includes in the Trust Fund "the rights under the Swap Administration Agreement relating to the Certificates," while the definition of Supplemental Interest Trust states that the Swap Administration Agreement, the Swap Agreement and the Swap Account "do not constitute parts of the Trust Fund." The two definitions cannot both be given effect as to those rights.

The allocation gives 93% to the Class A, M and B Certificates, 3% to the Class CE Certificates and 1% to each of the Class P, R-1, R-2, R-3 and RX Certificates, which totals 101% of the voting rights. Any vote requiring a specified percentage of Voting Rights cannot be computed as drafted.

The definition reads "the cap contract, dated Agreement Provider," omitting both the date and the counterparty to the Yield Maintenance Agreement. The instrument being incorporated is identified only by the Exhibit M-2 reference.

The recital says the Sellers conveyed "all the right, title and interest of the Sellers in and to the assets in the Mortgage Loans," a phrase that does not plainly convey the Mortgage Loans themselves as opposed to some subset of related assets. What passed from the Sellers to the Depositor is left to construction.

The Depositor conveys "the Trust Fund," but the Trust Fund definition includes the Special Deposit, which the last paragraph of Section 2.01 says is transferred by EMC, and rights under agreements to which the Depositor is not the counterparty. Whether those items passed under this granting clause requires reading it with the Trust Fund definition and Section 2.01's final paragraph.

The delivery obligation is imposed on the Depositor, yet the proviso permits "the Seller" to deliver substitute documents and the clause (x) certification is to be made by "the Seller or the title Servicer." Whose failure to deliver constitutes a document defect for purposes of Section 2.02 is left unclear.

This paragraph says the Special Deposit "will be transferred by EMC to the Trust" on the Closing Date, while the definition of Special Deposit says it is "deposited into the Trust by the Depositor" and Section 2.01's granting clause conveys the Trust Fund from the Depositor. Who made the deposit, and therefore whose conveyance carries it, cannot be reconciled.

The Custodian must report documents that "appear to be defective on its face," a standard the Agreement nowhere defines and which the same sentence pairs with a right to "conclusively rely" on execution and genuineness. What counts as a reportable document defect, which drives the cure/repurchase remedy in Section 2.02(c), is left to construction.

The Final Certification exceptions must be notified only to "the Sellers," although Section 2.02(c) and (d) make the related Originator equally liable to cure, repurchase or substitute for document defects. The Originator receives no notice under this subsection even though its obligation is triggered by the same defect.

The last sentence makes cure, repurchase or substitution "the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf," without saying whether it bars money damages for a refusal to perform that obligation, and it omits the Trustee from the list of persons limited. The scope of the sole-remedy limitation is squarely open to argument.

The Trustee's duty to enforce the Sellers' repurchase obligations must be read against Section 10 of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement, which makes cure, purchase or substitution "the Purchaser's, the Trustee's and the Certificateholder's sole and exclusive remedy" and fixes when a cause of action accrues. What the Trustee may enforce, and when, cannot be determined from this subsection alone.

The duty to give "prompt written notice" of a discovered breach is undefined as to time and says nothing about whether notice is a condition precedent to any repurchase obligation or an independent covenant whose breach is actionable. Both the meaning of "prompt" and the consequence of failing to give notice are left open.

The notice duty concerns breaches of representations "set forth in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement or any Bring Down Agreement," and must be squared with Section 10 of that agreement, which independently requires notice on discovery and then gives MSMCH 90 days to cure, purchase or substitute. Whether this Agreement's notice paragraph adds anything to, or triggers, the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement's protocol is contestable.

The bar on any substitution "following the second anniversary of the Closing Date" is stated to apply "[n]otwithstanding anything herein or in any other agreement to the contrary," but Section 2.05(a) suspends substitutions pending an Opinion of Counsel, which can push a required substitution past that deadline. The two provisions cannot both be given effect in that case.

The Purchase Price is due on "the Determination Date for the Distribution Date in the month following the month during which the related Seller or the related Originator became obligated to repurchase," but this Agreement never fixes when that obligation arises; Section 10 of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement sets a 90-day period running from discovery or notice. When a repurchase is late has to be worked out across the two instruments.

The survival clause says "the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2.03 hereof" survive delivery of the Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files, but Section 2.03 contains only Wells Fargo's corporate representations, while the loan-level warranties that survive delivery are in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and the Bring Down Agreements. What survives, and for whose benefit, must be read across those documents.

The representation is made "as of the Closing Date, following the transfer of the Mortgage Loans to it by the Seller," but is then stated in the past tense ("the Depositor had good title"), leaving the moment at which title and freedom from offsets is warranted unclear. It also warrants only as to "the Seller" in the singular although there are two Sellers.

The notice duty is triggered "[u]pon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach," with no conjunction and no mention of the Master Servicer, Securities Administrator or Custodians who hold the files. Which parties owe the notice obligation is left uncertain.

The opinion precondition applies "[n]otwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement" and can defer a repurchase or substitution indefinitely, which cannot be squared with Section 2.03's flat two-year bar on substitutions or with the 90-day cure-or-repurchase period in Section 10 of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement. Which timing rule prevails is left unresolved.

Substitution for a non-qualified mortgage is permitted only "if the conditions in Section 2.03 and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement or the Bring Down Agreements ... with respect to substitutions are satisfied," but Section 2.03 states no substitution conditions other than the two-year cutoff. The conditions to be satisfied must be assembled from the other agreements.

The final sentence forbids the Trust from engaging in any activity "other than in connection with the foregoing or other than as required or authorized by the terms of this Agreement while any Certificate is outstanding, and this Section 2.07," which is ungrammatical and leaves the restriction's content and duration uncertain. Whether the limitation lapses when no Certificate is outstanding cannot be read off the text.

This section requires the Master Servicer to "cause the Servicers to perform and observe" their covenants, an absolute obligation, while Section 4.03(b) limits the Master Servicer to enforcing those obligations and terminating a defaulting Servicer. Whether the Master Servicer guarantees Servicer performance or only polices it turns on reconciling the two sections.

The Trustee and Securities Administrator must "comply with any directions of the Seller, the Servicers or the Master Servicer" to preserve REMIC status, although the Seller is not a party to this Agreement and no standard limits such directions. The scope of that compliance duty, and how it interacts with the Trustee's own duties, is left open.

The closing sentence provides that nothing "shall impose any obligation on the part of the Trustee to assume or succeed to the duties or obligations of Wells Fargo or the Master Servicer unless the Trustee has not been able to find a successor servicer or a Successor master Servicer," so the exception swallows the disclaimer it qualifies. Whether the Trustee must step in is the opposite of what the sentence appears designed to say.

The fidelity bond and errors-and-omissions policy need only be "in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees," with no minimum amount, rating or benchmark. Whether coverage complies is unmeasurable on the face of the Agreement.

The obligation to return the Mortgage File is imposed by reference to "[s]uch trust receipt," although the preceding sentences describe only a request for release signed by a Servicing Officer and no trust receipt is provided for. The instrument creating the return obligation is unidentified.

The access sentence reads "The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access to information and documentation regarding the Mortgage Loans to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants at any time upon reasonable request," which omits conjunctions and leaves the class of persons entitled to access indeterminate. Who may demand the loan files under this subsection is a matter of construction.

Insurance collections are to be deposited "[p]ursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.04" and made subject to withdrawal "pursuant to Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04," although Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex and has nothing to do with insurance proceeds. The deposit and withdrawal mechanics point to the wrong sections.

The Master Servicer must use its "best reasonable efforts" to cause Servicers to keep primary mortgage insurance in force, a hybrid standard the Agreement never defines and which differs from the "Accepted Master Servicing Practices" standard used elsewhere. What level of effort discharges the duty is open.

Amounts collected under Primary Mortgage Insurance Policies are to be handled "[p]ursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05," but Article V of this Agreement ends at Section 5.04. The cited authority for the deposit does not exist.

The proviso permits prior reimbursement of "any such unreimbursed Monthly Advances," a term the Agreement does not define, whereas the first sentence speaks of "Advances" and "other unreimbursed advances." What may be recovered out of REO rental income is therefore uncertain.

The Master Servicer and Securities Administrator must deliver the Annual Statement of Compliance "to the Depositor and the Securities Administrator," so the Securities Administrator is directed to deliver to itself, and the certificate covers performance under "this Agreement or other applicable Servicing Agreement" to which these parties are not signatories. What each signatory is certifying is unclear.

A failure to comply with Section 4.16 is "deemed an Event of Default" requiring immediate termination without cure, which cannot be squared with the Event of Default definition and notice-and-cure regime of Section 9.01, and the paragraph then declares that it "shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement." Which regime governs termination of the Master Servicer must be decided.

This paragraph likewise makes any Section 4.17 failure an Event of Default mandating immediate termination and declares itself to supersede "any other provision in this Agreement," colliding with Section 9.01's Event of Default and cure provisions and with the identically worded supersession clauses in Sections 4.16 and 4.18. Two or more clauses each claim to override the others.

The Depositor's comment window runs to "the 12th calendar day after the Distribution Date" only if the Securities Administrator forwarded the draft by the 10th, while the Master Servicer must sign by the 13th and the filing is due within 15 days, so the deadlines can overlap or fail entirely if the draft is late. Whose duty is breached when the chain slips is left to the general contingency proviso.

The Master Servicer must sign the Form 8-K by the close of business on the 3rd Business Day after the Reportable Event, while the Depositor's approval or changes are due only "no later than the close of business on the 3rd Business Day," so signature may be required before the review period ends. The sequence of review and execution cannot be performed as written.

Item (IV) requires "a Sarbanes-Oxley Certification as described in Section 4.18(a)(ii)(D) below," but that certification is described in Section 4.18(a)(iii)(D); Section 4.18(a)(ii) concerns Form 8-K. The Form 10-K content requirement cites the wrong subsection.

The opening sentence is incomplete — "any Additional Form 10-D Disclosure, Additional Form 10- Disclosure or any Form 8-K Disclosure Information (collectively, the obligation to include such Additional Information..." — so the defined term "Additional Disclosure" is never actually defined even though the rest of the Agreement uses it. What information the obligation covers is unascertainable from the text.

Contribution is to be made "in such proportion as is appropriate to reflect the relative fault and the relative benefit of the respective parties," with no method for measuring either factor or for resolving a dispute about them. The clause supplies a standard without any means of applying it.

This paragraph deems any Section 4.18 failure an Event of Default requiring immediate termination and declares that it supersedes "any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary," while its own final sentence and Section 9.01's Event of Default regime say otherwise; it also refers to termination "pursuant to this Section 4.18(d)," which is the e-mail notice subsection. Which provision governs a reporting failure cannot be settled within the section.

Section 4.18 may be amended "[n]otwithstanding the provisions of Section 12.01" without Certificateholder consent, which cannot be squared with the amendment and consent requirements Section 12.01 imposes for the Agreement as a whole. Whether reporting obligations can be rewritten without holders is a question of which clause controls.

The parties agree their obligations "will be supplemented and modified as necessary" by evolving interpretations, market "convention or consensus," or "advice of counsel," and that "no amendment of this Agreement shall be required" to effect such changes. What a party is actually obliged to do at any given time is left indeterminate.

This section imposes the filing obligation on "the Seller," but EMC and the Sponsor are not parties to this Agreement under the preliminary paragraph, and no other provision makes them subject to its covenants. Whether anyone is bound to make the UCC filings requires reading this section against the parties clause and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement.

The last sentence says "[t]his right may be assigned by the Seller to a third party," although the option it describes is conferred on Saxon or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder and not on the Seller. Who may assign the optional purchase right is contradicted within the same paragraph.

The Swap Account is created and maintained by the Swap Administrator, yet this subsection provides that investments are made on the Majority Class CE Certificateholder's direction and that "[i]n the absence of written instructions to the Securities Administrator" amounts remain uninvested, and it also refers to funds "of the Trustee held pursuant to this Agreement." Who holds and invests the Swap Account is inconsistent within the paragraph.

This subsection has the Securities Administrator establish the Reserve Fund on or before the Closing Date, while the definition of Reserve Fund says it is created and maintained "pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof." Which provision governs the fund's creation, and thus its permitted withdrawals, must be reconciled.
